newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty meanders just below resistance, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty meanders just below resistance, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty remained anchored just below resistance levels in light early Wednesday trade with no strong buying or selling trends.

Dealers said expectations of a central bank intervention if the 2.5 percent from parity resistance was breached kept a tight cap on the zloty, while potential foreign entry into Polish treasuries was keeping the local unit underpinned.
"The zloty is drifting without much direction and there is no domestic pressure for the currency to rise or fall," said Leszek Szafranek, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
At 0845 GMT the zloty was at 2.49/2.46 percent from the parity rate, flat from opening at 2.51/2.46 and slightly weaker from Tuesday's close at 2.55/2.49 percent.
It was at 3.1520/30 to the dollar, down from Tuesday's close at 3.1460/75 and at 1.8504/14 to the mark, up from yesterday's 1.8515/30.

Dealers said international issues of zloty denonminated bonds, such as the European Investment Bank's (EIB) 100 million zloty tender announced on Tuesday, would not have a large impact on local forex trade, as payments were made in marks.

On the money market overnight rates held flat at opening levels of 22.30/22.55 percent in early trade but dealers said one-day rates may ease later in the day as the central bank refrained from draining the market on Wednesday.
By mid-day tomorrow/next rates slipped to 22.20/22.65 percent from Tuesday's close at 22.55/22.70 percent.
Foreign investors remained on the sidelines in early secondary T-bill market trade but dealers said some foregin bids for one-year paper could materialise later today.
